'''Gerald Feinberg''' (27 May 1933 – 21 April 1992) was a [[Columbia University]] [[physicist]], [[futurist]] and popular science author.  He spent a year as a Member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], and two years at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory|Brookhaven Laboratories]].<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1992/04/23/nyregion/gerald-feinberg-58-physicist-taught-at-columbia-university.html "Gerald Feinberg, 58, Physicist; Taught at Columbia University"]. Retrieved 2015-03-28.</ref> Feinberg went to [[Bronx High School of Science]] with [[Steven Weinberg]] and [[Sheldon Glashow]] and obtained his bachelor's and graduate degrees from [[Columbia University]].<ref>The Second Creation, Crease & Mann, Macmillan Publishing Company, 1986</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Columbia College (Columbia University). Office of Alumni Affairs and Development |url=http://archive.org/details/ldpd_12981092_030 |title=Columbia College today |last2=Columbia College (Columbia University) |date=1988 |publisher=New York, N.Y. : Columbia College, Office of Alumni Affairs and Development |others=Columbia University Libraries}}</ref> His father was Yiddish poet and journalist [[Leon Feinberg]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|date=23 January 1969|title=Leon Feinberg, 71, Yiddish Journalist|volume=CXVIII|page=27|work=[[The New York Times]]|issue=40542|location=New York, N.Y.|url=https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1969/01/23/77323538.pdf}}</ref> Among his students were [[Scott Dodelson]], physicist at [[Carnegie Mellon University]].

==Research==

He coined the term [[tachyon]] for hypothetical [[faster-than-light]] particles and analysed their [[quantum field theory|quantum field]] properties,<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=G. Feinberg
 |year=1967
 |title=Possibility of Faster-Than-Light Particles
 |journal=[[Physical Review]]
 |volume=159 |issue=5
 |pages=1089–1105
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.159.1089
|bibcode = 1967PhRv..159.1089F }}</ref> predicted the existence of the [[muon neutrino]]<ref>
{{cite book
 |author=M. Schwartz
 |year=1992
 |title=Nobel Lectures
 |page=469
 |publisher=[[World Scientific]]
 |isbn=
}}</ref> and advocated [[cryonics]] as a public service.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=G. Feinberg
 |year=1966
 |title=Physics and Life Prolongation
 |journal=[[Physics Today]]
 |volume=19 |issue=11 |pages=45–48
 |doi=10.1063/1.3047814
|bibcode = 1966PhT....19k..45F }}</ref>  He was a member of the [[Foresight Institute]]'s advisory panel.<ref>{{cite journal
 |author=D. Shafer
 |year=1990
 |title=Feinberg Anxious for Policy Discussions
 |url=http://www.foresight.org/Updates/Update09/Update09.1.html#anchor1358298
 |journal=Foresight Update
 |volume=9
 |pages=1
 |access-date=2007-04-23
 |archive-date=2019-10-23
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191023131354/https://foresight.org/Updates/Update09/Update09.1.html#anchor1358298
 |url-status=dead
 }}</ref>

===Parapsychology===

Feinberg wrote a foreword to [[Edgar Mitchell]]'s book ''Psychic Explorations'' (1974) in which he endorsed [[psychic|psychic phenomena]]. His concept of a tachyon, a theoretical particle that travels faster than the speed of light has been advocated by some parapsychologists who claim that it could explain [[precognition]] or [[psychokinesis]]. However, there is no scientific evidence tachyon particles exist and such paranormal claims have been described as pseudoscientific.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.csicop.org/sb/show/tachyons_and_other_nonentities|title= Tachyons and Other Nonentities|publisher= [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]] |journal= [[Skeptical Inquirer]] |author=Rothman, Milton|date= September 1994|accessdate= 2014-03-16 |volume= 4|issue= 3|author-link= Milton A. Rothman}}</ref><ref>[[Robert Todd Carroll|Carroll, Robert Todd]]. (2003). ''[[The Skeptic's Dictionary|The Skeptic's Dictionary: A Collection of Strange Beliefs, Amusing Deceptions, and Dangerous Delusions]]''. Wiley. pp. 370-371. {{ISBN|0-471-27242-6}}</ref>
